lead: The largest lake in Spain, the cradle of paella and the most spectacular sunset on the Mediterranean. Just 15 minutes from Valencia, nature in its purest state.

The Albufera is not just a lake: it is the result of centuries of coexistence between people and nature, where water and rice become the great protagonists of the landscape and of Valencian culture. Fishermen, farmers and migratory birds share this unique space that changes colour with the seasons: green in summer, golden in autumn during the harvest, flooded blue in winter when it serves as a refuge for birds.
It is a destination for all year round, although autumn — with the rice fields ripe and the greatest concentration of birdlife — is the most special time. Access to the park is free.

items.kicker: Essential experience · El Saler and El Palmar jetties
items.title: Boat Trip on the Lake
items.subtitle: Quiet electric boats · 60 min · Gola del Pujol · Park canals
items.body: The boat trip is the most complete and recommended experience for getting to know the Albufera. From the jetties at El Saler and El Palmar — the most popular of the park’s six municipal jetties — local boatmen guide you through the canals, the Gola del Pujol and the open areas of the lake. The guides interpret the landscape: water management, the rice cycle, traditional fishing, birdlife and the history of an ecosystem that has been transforming for more than 1,200 years. The electric boats are quiet and emission-free, which lets you get close to the birds without scaring them. The municipal boats are also an economical option (€4–5 with no advance booking).
facts: Jetties
El Saler and El Palmar · 6 municipal jetties in total across the park
Duration
40–60 min municipal trip · 75–90 min sunset excursion with a guide
Municipal price
€4–5 · No advance booking · Guided by local boatmen
Guided excursion
Electric boats · Bilingual guides · From visitalbufera.com

items.title: Sunset over the Lake
items.subtitle: The only place in the Comunitat where the sun sets over the water · Autumn: the best time
items.body: The Albufera is the only place in the Comunitat Valenciana where the sun sets over the water, creating one of the most spectacular sunsets on the Mediterranean. The Arabs poetically called the lake “the mirror of the sun”. Watching the sunset from a boat in the middle of the lake — when the engine stops and silence reigns, and the sky turns orange and violet over the calm water — is one of the most memorable moments of a visit to Valencia. Autumn is the best time: the ripe rice fields create a palette of golds, birdlife is at its peak and the sunsets are especially spectacular. Places for the sunset trip often sell out at weekends: book in advance.
facts: Best time to visit
Autumn (Sep–Nov) · Golden rice fields + peak birdlife + spectacular skies
Excursion length
75–90 min from the jetty · Engine switched off in the middle of the lake
Booking
Booking in advance is essential, especially at weekends
Fact
The only place in the Comunitat where the sun sets over the water

items.kicker: Lakeside village · Cradle of Valencian paella
items.title: El Palmar · Food and Barracas
items.subtitle: Valencian paella · All i pebre of eel · Traditional 18th-century barracas
items.body: El Palmar is the heart of the Albufera: a small island surrounded by rice fields and canals where the traditional economy based on fishing and rice growing is still alive. The village is famous as the cradle of Valencian paella: it was in these rice fields that the farmworkers created the original recipe with chicken, rabbit, vegetables and snails. The restaurants of El Palmar are a must-stop: the all i pebre of lake eels (with fishing techniques with 600 years of tradition), arroz a banda and arroz al senyoret are unique dishes. The traditional 18th-century barracas — reed-roofed buildings — are another symbol of the village that Blasco Ibáñez immortalised in his novel “Cañas y Barro” (1902).
facts: Gastronomy
Authentic Valencian paella · All i pebre of eel · Arroz a banda · Arroz al senyoret
Recommended restaurants
Bon Aire (paella benchmark) · Nou Racó (lake views) · Ca Teresa (El Saler)
Barracas
Traditional reed-roofed houses · Some can be visited · Ethnological heritage
Blasco Ibáñez
“Cañas y Barro” (1902) · The most important Valencian novel set in the Albufera

items.title: Birdwatching
items.subtitle: Flamingos · Herons · Ducks · Marsh harrier · Racó de l’Olla observatory
items.body: The Albufera is one of the most important wetlands on the Iberian Peninsula for birdlife. A Ramsar site and Special Protection Area for Birds (SPA) within the Natura 2000 network, it is the permanent or transit home of more than 300 species. Between October and March birdlife is at its peak: up to 30,000 birds can gather in the wetlands. In May, thousands of flamingos rest during their migration. The Racó de l’Olla Observatory (free access, observation towers, specialist staff) is the best spot for birdwatching. The first hours of the day and sunset are the best times.
facts: Species
Flamingo, grey heron, little egret, cormorant, marsh harrier, tern, duck
Best time to visit
Oct–Mar: peak concentration · May: thousands of migratory flamingos
Observatory
Racó de l’Olla · Free access · Observation towers · Specialist staff
Protection
Ramsar site + SPA + Natura 2000 Network · Natural Park since 1986

items.kicker: A landscape in transformation · 14,000 hectares of cultivation
items.title: The Rice Fields · The Marjal and the Rice Cycle
items.subtitle: Green in summer · Golden in autumn · Flooded blue in winter
items.body: The rice fields occupy 70% of the Natural Park’s surface — about 14,000 hectares — and are the real vital engine of the ecosystem. The marjal (marshland) is a landscape in constant transformation whose colour changes with the seasons: bright green in summer when the rice grows, golden in autumn during the harvest (September–October), blue in winter when the fields are flooded to serve as a refuge for migratory birds, and brown at the end of winter when the tractors prepare the land. The “tancats” — artificial wetlands such as La Pipa (40 ha) or L’Illa — can be visited by prior booking and are habitats of great biodiversity.
facts: Size
14,000 ha of rice fields · 70% of the total surface of the park
Cycle
Summer: green · Autumn: golden (harvest Sep–Oct) · Winter: flooded blue
Tancats
La Pipa (40 ha) · L’Illa · Visitable by prior booking · High biodiversity
Varieties
DO Valencia rice: Senia, Bomba and Albufera · Protected Designation of Origin

items.kicker: Mediterranean forest · The barrier between the lake and the sea
items.title: La Devesa del Saler and the Dunes
items.subtitle: Pine forests · Natural dunes · Cycle route · Cycle lane between rice fields
items.body: La Devesa del Saler is the strip of land — the “restringa” — that separates the Albufera lake from the Mediterranean. With Mediterranean pine forests, dwarf fan palms, mastic trees, kermes oaks and a dune system of great ecological value, it is the most impressive natural space in the park for cycling and hiking lovers. The cycle lane that crosses La Devesa connects El Saler with the lake, the beaches and El Palmar. At visitalbufera.com you can hire bikes and e-bikes with well-signposted routes. The “bike + boat pack” is the most popular combination: pedal through forest and beach in the morning, sail on the lake at sunset.
facts: Ecosystem
Aleppo pine, dwarf fan palm, mastic tree, rosemary, thyme · Protected dune system
Cycle lane
From El Saler to El Palmar via La Devesa · Signposted and flat
Bike hire
visitalbufera.com · Bikes and e-bikes · Bike + Boat Pack available
Dunes
Malladas and viewpoints with views of the lake and the Mediterranean at the same time

blocks.title: Tips for visiting the Albufera
items: The sunset boat trip is the most memorable experience — always book ahead at weekends
Paella in El Palmar on Sundays is a Valencian tradition: book a table on Saturday so you do not miss out
Autumn is the best time: golden rice fields + flamingos + movie-style sunsets
Bring binoculars: the Racó de l’Olla Observatory has free access and is the best birdwatching spot
The bike + boat pack from visitalbufera.com is the perfect combination for the whole day: morning by bike through La Devesa, afternoon on the boat
EMT buses 24 and 25 are free with the Valencia Tourist Card and go straight to El Palmar
